notes: BANK CHARGES AND INTEREST NOW GO INTO THE LEDGER, FROM THE RECONCILIATION ITSELF. Until now, a bank charge you had not yet recorded could be typed into Other adjustments on the bank reconciliation, the difference driven to zero, and the month signed off — while the ledger still had no charge, the bank account was still overstated by it, and the expense never reached the Income and Expenditure statement. The same adjustment then had to be retyped every month, for ever, because the thing it made up for was never recorded. Each adjustment row now has the account it belongs to and a BOOK button. Press it and the entry is posted on the STATEMENT DATE — the charge to the expense account you chose, interest to the income account — and the row disappears, because once it is in the ledger no adjustment is needed. YOUR RECONCILIATION DOES NOT MOVE WHEN YOU DO THIS: booking shifts the cashbook by exactly the amount the adjustment was supplying, so a month that balanced still balances. A genuine bank ERROR still belongs in Other adjustments and should stay there — the bank will reverse it, and there is nothing for you to record. The screen now says which is which. THE SIGN WAS DOCUMENTED BACKWARDS. The rule is, and always was: a positive adjustment increases the statement toward the cashbook, a negative one decreases it. The hint under the table then said the opposite — that unbooked bank charges are "usually negative". They are POSITIVE: the bank has taken money your cashbook still shows. Interest not yet booked is NEGATIVE. Following the old hint pushed the difference further out, and then you were hunting for an error that was the hint's. Corrected, with the reasoning shown rather than just the instruction. Nothing else changed in this release.
